rationale.complete: Round 1 done: synthetic validation (12 scenarios x 25 runs), 14 per-period verdicts with dated predictions, NE09 test, counterfactual simulations, post hoc short-lag and shared-label checks, and a scorecard. The frozen holdout test (#22, #28, #45) is written and dry-run, not run. Round 1b (2026-10-04): re-run on context-ledger visibility for 14 periods, a work-commit switch variant (8 periods), an NE09 blind-window native and a #31 work-wave native.
rationale.faithfulness: The core claim (links drive switches) fails its primary timing test (3/11 herding periods beat the link time-shift null) and its signature: future links predict switches better than past links (pooled -1.17 +- 0.30), naive agents show a 3.3x pre-trend, NE09 failed. What survives is a strong, well-calibrated association (pooled HR 2.3), simple rather than complex contagion, and directed recruitment only in own-artifact weeks. Round 1b: pre-NE09 weeks were mismeasured (5/11 now beat the shift null, card-level P1 mixed), but lead > lag persists (-1.04 +- 0.24) and switches are elevated before the link can be read (6.5x vs 3.5x after), so links mark bursts; NE09's premise is void; work switches repeat the pattern.
rationale.usefulness: It answers an operator question with numbers: throttling link-sharing would trim peak pile-ons by at most ~20% (upper bound), so act on ownership or burst triggers instead. The lead/lag diagnostic and the lambda / R_link bounds are cheap to compute from any swarm's logs. But the counterfactual is model-based (+-0.1) and not interventionally validated.

one_line: Links co-move with project switches (HR 2.6), but recipients switch before they can read them: links mark bursts; removal trims peaks at most 30%.
